items.title: So bullish on MCP
items.text: So bullish on MCP. Its utility exceeds the "M" part: even AI aside, it'll be a civilization-scale accomplishment to get all our systems communicating through one universal open protocol. A missing piece was how to get arbitrary callbacks across sessions. MCP could read and write, but it couldn't tell you later "this event happened." MCP Events fixes this. We're adding support in our own MCP. Say an agent makes a deployment, and wants to know when it's complete. Instead of polling, it can subscribe to 𝚍𝚎𝚙𝚕𝚘𝚢𝚖𝚎𝚗𝚝.𝚜𝚞𝚌𝚌𝚎𝚎𝚍𝚎𝚍. PSA: With Vercel Queues and Workflows, writing the backend machinery for your own MCPs to do this is easy peasy.

items.title: If you are a product leader, here is a simple exercise: draw out your product lifecycle
items.text: If you are a product leader, here is a simple exercise: draw out your product lifecycle. e.g. market understanding -> design -> development -> GTM. Chances are your PMs spend more time in some stages than others - because of the nature of your product, your org or their comfort zones. This is a handoff-heavy, lossy process. Now ask yourself: using AI, how much deeper can PMs go on every stage? PMs should be able to - build a much deeper, broader understanding of users and the market - iterate fast from ideas to working prototypes - explore the codebase to study technical constraints and tradeoffs - run their own analytics and investigate questions as they emerge - understand the GTM funnel...
